top5.why: Core signature loop appears identical to audited Safe 1.3.0 with ordered-owner and contract-signature bounds checks.
Nonce, guard and gas-refund flow matches canonical 1.3.0.
Guarded by threshold==0 so it cannot be re-run on initialized proxies.
Only enabled modules may execute, per standard design.
Calls a user-supplied callback after deployment, but it has no effect on Safe funds.
Mints and adds LP against spot reserves checked only within 0.5% of a short TWAP, so a small sandwich is possible.
Burns LP and redeems at spot reserves with the same loose TWAP bounds.
Anyone can reset the TWAP snapshot to push the enter/exit time window out of range.
Arbitrary call by gov or any subgov, a privileged-key risk rather than an attacker bug.
Votes come from external incentivizer contracts that are trusted for vote accounting.
Admin-only upgrade with delegatecall, standard hardhat-deploy proxy.
Admin-gated, with no two-step transfer.
Delegatecalls init data to the implementation, reachable only by admin or the constructor.
Gated by onlyProxyAdmin.
EIP-1967 slots are used, so no collision.
Share price and pool amounts come from the manipulable spot slot0 tick, so a flash-loan price skew mints mispriced shares and drains LPs.
Redeems against current spot-composition positions and pushes funds before the share burn and sender check, so it can be sandwiched.
Owner-controlled swap with no price limit or slippage check, and fee variables are swapped between the base and limit positions.
Callback authorises only on msg.sender==pool and pays from the payer encoded in data.
Computes totals from spot-price-dependent liquidity amounts that deposit relies on.
Complex accounting of restoring or re-adding liquidity and the insolvency check could mis-account held ETH and tokens.
Refunds w.eth to the owner depending on price movement and relies on solvency checks.
Hand-rolled linked-list segment bookkeeping can desync from pool liquidity.
The refund subtraction and uint96/uint104 casts can revert and lock user purchases.
Partial-fill rounding loops can mis-charge by one tick unit.
Standard Safe proxy delegatecall forwarder with the singleton in slot 0.
Checks for a nonzero singleton.
The initializer is called in the same transaction, so there is no front-run window.
Callback is caller-supplied but does not affect the proxy.
CREATE2 salt derives from the initializer hash and nonce.
Mixed ERC20/721 accounting with whitelist skips could desync NFT and token balances.
Values up to 50 wei are treated as NFT ids, and an id of 0 or ERC20 dust amounts are ambiguous.
Cross-chain mint reverts if the per-chain ERC20 supply cap would be exceeded, which could strand bridged tokens.
Whitelist toggling can leave NFT and ERC20 balances inconsistent.
Overloaded approve routes by value, so small allowances are treated as NFT ids.
Permissionless solve with a caller-chosen solver, but each user is paid exactly their own signed atomicPrice.
Does not validate a nonzero price or balance, so users may set bad requests against themselves.
Rounds down in the solver's favour by at most one wei.
View-only helper that may diverge from the actual solve.
View-only validity check.
Reward per token is totalRewards/totalSupply with a changing supply, so tokens minted later claim past rewards and can leave the contract insolvent.
receivedAirdrop is never set and ids use nextTokenId+i, so the batch can revert or repeat and increases supply, diluting the reward math.
The view ignores the computed totalRewards_ and uses stale totalRewards.
Transfers are locked per token unless the owner is msg.sender, which bypasses the unlock fee.
Sends ETH to the fee destination before setting transferUnlocked.
